summary: This note is a collection of passages from the Wikipedia article on Myanmar (Burma), covering its geography, name origins, history from early Pyu and Mon civilisations through the Toungoo and Konbaung dynasties, British colonial rule, independence and military rule, and the post-2010 reforms. It also covers administrative divisions, demographics and religion, ethnic conflicts, foreign relations, the economy (stock exchange, gems), education and tourism.
one_line: Overview of Myanmar (Burma): its history, ethnic and religious makeup, politics and reforms since 2010, foreign relations, economy, and tourism.
key_facts: Myanmar, officially the Republic of the Union of Myanmar and also known as Burma, is a Southeast Asian state bordered by Bangladesh, India, China, Laos and Thailand; its capital is Naypyidaw and its largest city is Yangon (Rangoon).
Myanmar covers 676,578 square kilometres, and its 2014 census recorded 51 million people, much lower than expected.
Myanmar is divided into seven states and seven regions; regions are predominantly Bamar, while states are home to particular ethnic minorities.
Hanthawaddy forces sacked Ava in 1752, ending the 266-year-old Toungoo Dynasty.

Under British administration Myanmar was the second-wealthiest country in South-East Asia and the world's largest rice exporter; British Burma began exporting crude oil in 1853 and produced 75% of the world's teak.
Myanmar became independent in 1948 as a democracy; after a coup d'état in 1962 it became a military dictatorship under the Burma Socialist Programme Party.

The 1988 8888 Uprising was crushed by security forces, and General Saw Maung's coup created the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), which renamed the country the 'Union of Myanmar' in 1989.
The military junta was officially dissolved in 2011 after the 2010 general election, and in the 2015 election Aung San Suu Kyi's party won a majority in both houses, ending military rule.
Hillary Clinton visited in December 2011, the first visit by a US Secretary of State in more than fifty years, and the US announced resumption of diplomatic relations on 13 January 2012.
Thein Sein visited the White House in May 2013, the first Myanmar president to do so in 47 years, since Ne Win in September 1966.
Myanmar has been an ASEAN member since 1997 and chaired the forum and hosted the summit in 2014.
The Yangon Stock Exchange officially opened on 25 March 2016, with First Myanmar Investment Co., Ltd. the first stock traded at 26,000 kyats ($22).
Pew Research reports 7% of the population is Christian and 4% Muslim, though independent researchers put the Muslim population at 6 to 10%.
Ongoing conflicts as of October 2012 included the Kachin conflict, the Rohingya conflict in Rakhine State, and conflicts with Shan, Lahu and Karen groups in the east.
